title: Magnetic-Levitation Shuttle for Weft Insertion: Electromagnetic Modeling, Wireless Displacement Sensing, and PID Stabilization
content: Conventional torsion-axis projectile looms suffer from low weft-insertion efficiency and high mechanical loss. This paper presents a magnetic-levitation shuttle weft-insertion system in which a permanent-magnet shuttle is suspended and guided without contact by an 8-pole U-shaped electromagnetic track. An Ampere-loop-based magnetic-circuit model with permanent-magnet magnetomotive force is derived, giving the nonlinear force law \( F=k i_{eq}^2/x_{eq}^2 \) and the coupled mechanical-electrical dynamics. Because the open-loop plant has a right-half-plane pole, a wireless Hall displacement sensor is integrated on the shuttle for real-time gap feedback, and a PID controller is tuned from the linearized current/stiffness model. Co-simulations in MATLAB/Simulink and ten reciprocating weft-insertion tests on a 0-12 m platform show that, at Kp=3.0, Ki=5.0, Kd=0.2, the system achieves closed-loop stability with 0.2s settling time, 5% overshoot, and positioning accuracy within ±1.5 mm. The results demonstrate that contactless magnetic-levitation actuation combined with lightweight wireless sensing is feasible for high-speed textile weft insertion.
